content: Ceftaroline is an antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections, including community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) and acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI), including those caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). It belongs to the cephalosporin class of antibiotics and is administered intravenously. Indications and Dosage: 1. For Adults (≥18 years): CABP: 600 mg IV every 12 hours for 5–7 days. ABSSSI: 600 mg IV every 12 hours for 5–14 days. 2. For Pediatric Patients: CABP: Ages 2 months to <2 years: 8 mg/kg IV every 8 hours for 5–14 days. Ages ≥2 years to <18 years (≤33 kg): 12 mg/kg IV every 8 hours for 5–14 days. Ages ≥2 years to <18 years (>33 kg): 400 mg IV every 8 hours or 600 mg IV every 12 hours for 5–14 days. ABSSSI: Birth to <2 months: 6 mg/kg IV every 8 hours for 5–14 days. Ages 2 months to <2 years: 8 mg/kg IV every 8 hours for 5–14 days. Ages ≥2 years to <18 years (≤33 kg): 12 mg/kg IV every 8 hours for 5–14 days. Ages ≥2 years to <18 years (>33 kg): 400 mg IV every 8 hours or 600 mg IV every 12 hours for 5–14 days. Administration: Ceftaroline is administered via intravenous infusion over 5–60 minutes in adults and children aged >2 months. For children aged <2 months, the infusion duration is 30–60 minutes. The solution should be prepared by mixing with 0.9% NaCl, D5W, or lactated Ringer’s injection. The final solution should be clear to light or dark yellow, depending on concentration and storage conditions. Storage: Unopened vials should be stored at 25°C (77°F), with permissible excursions to 15–30°C (59–86°F). Precautions: Allergies: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to ceftaroline, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or any other substances. Renal Impairment: Dosage adjustments are necessary for patients with renal impairment to avoid adverse neurological reactions such as encephalopathy or seizures. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: There is no data on the use of ceftaroline in pregnant women or its presence in human milk. Consult your doctor for guidance. Vaccines: Ceftaroline may reduce the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). Avoid administering live vaccines during treatment. Drug Interactions: BCG and Typhoid Vaccines: Ceftaroline decreases the efficacy of these live vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Vaccination should be delayed until after antibiotic treatment is completed. Cholera Vaccine: Avoid coadministration with systemic antibiotics, as they may inactivate the vaccine strain. Aminoglycosides (e.g., amikacin, gentamicin, tobramycin): Ceftaroline may increase nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. Use with caution and monitor closely. Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (e.g., atezolizumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab): Coadministration may interfere with therapeutic effects. Use caution and monitor. Probenecid: Increases ceftaroline levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use with caution. Oral Microbiota Products: Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of these products by decreasing bacterial spore activity. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota therapy. Side Effects: Common side effects include pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site, nausea, and diarrhea. Rare but serious side effects include severe intestinal conditions caused by Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which may occur during or after treatment. Prolonged use may lead to oral thrush or vaginal yeast infections. Severe allergic reactions are rare but require immediate medical attention. Overdose: In case of overdose with serious symptoms (e.g., loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing), call emergency services (911) or a poison control center immediately. Notes: Laboratory tests (e.g., kidney function) may be required during treatment. Complete the full course of therapy as prescribed, even if symptoms improve early. Consult your healthcare provider for any missed doses or storage instructions. Ceftaroline is a potent antibiotic that should be used judiciously to prevent the development of drug-resistant bacteria. Always follow your healthcare provider’s instructions for safe and effective use.
